body:
CLAIM CANDIDATES
C-PWA-01 [supported, high]: Automatic multi-display enumeration/placement is a Chromium-desktop-only enhancement; Firefox and Safari need manual stage placement. Evidence: W3C Window Management + MDN BCD Window/Screen/ScreenDetails.
C-PWA-02 [supported, high]: One control click cannot reliably open arbitrary multiple windows; each `window.open()` generally needs a distinct user gesture. The Window Management spec's targeted-fullscreen handoff permits only a narrow fullscreen+one-popup flow.
C-PWA-03 [supported, high]: Fullscreen must be requested by the active document under transient user activation; a controller cannot remotely fullscreen a cross-origin stage via WSS.
C-PWA-04 [supported, high]: Security-first architecture should isolate public stage origin/storage/SW/cookies from trusted controller/mic/AI origin and use capability-scoped WSS; strict COOP intentionally forfeits WindowProxy lifecycle control.
C-PWA-05 [supported]: Permissions API state is advisory/aggregate, descriptor support differs, it cannot revoke, and every capability invocation still needs exception handling.
C-PWA-06 [supported, high]: Microphone capture requires a secure, eligible context and explicit permission; it belongs only on trusted controller origin and must stop tracks when inactive.
C-PWA-07 [supported, high]: Service worker update lifecycle can leave multiple open presentation windows on different app versions; updates should be gated before a session rather than forced mid-session.
C-PWA-08 [supported]: PWA installation does not imply offline cloud AI/WSS, Window Management support, or removal of gesture/permission rules.
C-PWA-09 [supported]: `beforeinstallprompt` is Chromium-only/non-standard; install UX must be feature/platform specific.
C-PWA-10 [supported]: Manifest fullscreen mode and Fullscreen API are separate states; use standalone for controller, explicit fullscreen for stage.

OBSERVATION CANDIDATES
O-PWA-01 W3C Window Management: `isExtended` exposed in secure contexts without prompt; detailed screens may prompt; denial/policy causes NotAllowedError. https://www.w3.org/TR/window-management/
O-PWA-02 MDN BCD: getScreenDetails/ScreenDetails Chrome 100+, Edge mirror, Firefox/Safari false; ScreenDetails false on Chrome Android. https://github.com/mdn/browser-compat-data/tree/main/api
O-PWA-03 MDN Window Management usage: modern browsers require separate gesture per open; recommends one-at-a-time/reuse/recovery UI. https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Window_Management_API/Using
O-PWA-04 Fullscreen standard: transient activation and fullscreen policy/support checks are normative. https://fullscreen.spec.whatwg.org/
O-PWA-05 MDN Window.open: popup block returns null; COOP BCG separation yields severed WindowProxy that reports closed=true. https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Window/open
O-PWA-06 MDN Same-origin/BroadcastChannel/SW register: subdomains differ; BroadcastChannel and SW registrations do not span them. https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/Security/Same-origin_policy ; https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Broadcast_Channel_API ; https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/ServiceWorkerContainer/register
O-PWA-07 MDN getUserMedia: secure context, top-level/delegated origin, always permission, required indicators. https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/MediaDevices/getUserMedia
O-PWA-08 MDN SW lifecycle: waiting activation plus optional skipWaiting/clients.claim creates explicit update-coordination choices. https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Service_Worker_API/Using_Service_Workers
O-PWA-09 Chrome install criteria: fetch-handler requirement removed in Chrome 108 mobile/112 desktop. https://developer.chrome.com/blog/update-install-criteria
O-PWA-10 MDN/WebKit: install affordances differ sharply across Chromium desktop, Safari 17 Add to Dock, desktop Firefox, Android, and iOS 16.4+. https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/Progressive_web_apps/Guides/Making_PWAs_installable ; https://webkit.org/blog/14445/webkit-features-in-safari-17-0/ ; https://webkit.org/blog/13966/webkit-features-in-safari-16-4/

EXPANSION LEADS CLOSED
- Separate-origin conflict: closed with security-first split-origin verdict and explicit COOP tradeoff.
- Targeted fullscreen compatibility: closed as experimental/Chromium enhancement; local gesture mandatory.
- Service-worker-as-install-requirement: closed/refuted as universal claim; current Chrome and Edge can install without one.
- Installability-vs-capabilities coupling: closed/refuted; installation grants none of Window Management/mic/fullscreen powers.
- Cross-browser custom install prompt: closed/refuted; Chromium-only.
- Mobile multi-screen: closed as non-product-grade due interface/event BCD gaps.
- Cross-origin audience remote fullscreen: closed/refuted; user activation does not cross WSS/opener boundary.

No material open lead remains in the assigned axes. A hardware/browser manual test matrix would validate vendor behavior but would not change the standards-based architecture verdict.

## EXPAND
summary: Claim candidates, observations, and exhausted expansion leads
